title: Base change for a composite square
statement:
Consider a tower of Cartesian diagrams of schemes

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
W & \xleftarrow{j} & Z\\
i\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow k\\
X & \xleftarrow{h} & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{g} & T
\end{array}
$$

and let $K\in D(T_{\Et})$. If

$$
f^{-1}Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_*e^{-1}K
\quad\text{and}\quad
i^{-1}Rh_*e^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rj_*k^{-1}e^{-1}K
$$

are isomorphisms, then
$(f\circ i)^{-1}Rg_*K\to Rj_*(e\circ k)^{-1}K$ is an isomorphism
(``the outer rectangle'') and the analogous statement holds
degreewise for an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $T_{\Et}$ and the maps
$R^q$.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma [Tag `0EZS`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZS).*)
The derived maps here are the unbounded exchange morphisms of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$; the degreewise maps are those of [sbc-def-base-change-map], for each integer $q\ge0$, without requiring isomorphisms in other degrees.

proof.text: Work directly with the existing unbounded module-coefficient source-library functors L(upperStar A a), their composition isomorphisms leftDerivedUpperStarComp, and derivedSquareUpperStarIso. The three rearrangements of leftDerivedUpperStarComp_assoc' in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.Derived.UpperStarCompCoherence give horizontal pasting of the derived square isomorphisms: expand the square as the inverse comparison through the diagonal followed by the other comparison, apply the three associativity rearrangements and cancel hom-inv pairs. This is the private theorem unbounded_derivedSquareUpperStarIso_paste_horiz_hom. It works for any two commutative squares and thus needs no pullback-pasting theorem.

Package the preceding equality as a TwoSquare equality. Apply mateEquiv_whiskerTop_whiskerBottom and mateEquiv_vcomp to obtain unbounded_derivedBaseChangeSquare_paste_horiz. Evaluate at K to obtain unbounded_derivedBaseChangeMap_paste_horiz_app: the outer exchange is the source composition comparison, L(i inverse-image) of the lower exchange, the upper exchange at L(e inverse-image)K, and derived j direct image of the inverse target comparison.

For the unbounded assertion, specialize the pasting equality to lower.toCommSq.flip and upper.toCommSq.flip. Both outside factors are isomorphisms; the lower middle factor is a functor applied to the hypothesized lower isomorphism and the upper middle factor is the hypothesized upper isomorphism. Functors and composition preserve isomorphisms.

For the independent degree-q assertion set K=F[0]. The existing unbounded comparison leftDerivedUpperStarHomologyFunctorIso A i q and NatIso.isIso_map_iff show that Hq(Li*(lower exchange)) is invertible from hLower. Let c be (singleFunctorCompLeftDerivedUpperStarIso A e).app F, identifying Le*(F[0]) with (e*F)[0]. Naturality of the upper exchange expresses its component at Le*(F[0]) as its component at (e*F)[0] conjugated by the functor images of c.hom and c.inv. Apply Hq; the middle factor is hUpper and the outside factors are functor images of isomorphisms. Finally apply Hq to the pasting equality and use functoriality and composition of isomorphisms. No hypothesis in any other degree is used.

proof.text:
The composites of the two base-change maps of
[sbc-def-base-change-map] are the mates of the same composite of
the identification isomorphisms $\theta_\square$ of the two pasted
squares; the associativity and triangle identities for the
inverse-image–direct-image adjunctions (the identity and pasting laws
recorded in [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting], applied with
the roles of the vertical and horizontal sides interchanged) show that
this mate is exactly the base-change map of the outer rectangle, so the
composite of the two isomorphisms is the required isomorphism.
